text: Christians who want to appeal to context to try to overrule the plain sense of a given biblical passage will frequently appeal to this notion of the picture on
the box the idea being that we can't properly interpret a given passage until we know how it fits into the broader
context namely the overall message of the whole Bible and that is what is comparable to a jigsaw puzzle therefore
to know where the pieces fit we have to look at the picture on the box and this is problematic for a number of reasons and probably the biggest is that there's
no such thing as a picture on the box not only does the bible not have a single overall message but in order to
generate your own single overall message you have to put together the constituent Parts but if you don't understand where
they go until you already have the overall message then it's hopelessly circular and you can never generate the
overall message and this is because again the Bible has no overall message but what people are confusing for the picture on the box is actually just the
dogmas the ideologies of the given religious tradition in other words you're just saying that whatever your
tradition insists the Bible's overall message is is the picture on the box so you're imposing a unifying interpretive
framework on the Bible that comes from your tradition that you have inherited from those who came before so that is
coming from out outside the Bible a far better metaphor for how we interpret the Bible is a toy box full of Lego blocks
and not just one set numerous different sets some of them complete some of them not also numerous straight pieces that
may or may not have come originally from a set and we can try to create a single message out of all of these but we're going to have a bunch of pieces left
over and you're going to have fences from Jurassic Park combined with panels from the Millennium Falcon and you're going to have Dumbledore's head on
Gandalf's body and it's going to be a Frankenstein's monster of pieces but you have absolutely no other option if you
want to try to construct a single message and that's what happens with the Bible a much better approach would be to
try to understand each individual set on its own terms what were the engineers trying to accomplish do we have all the
pieces what has changed between the original creation of this set and the pieces that have come down to us what's
left over do these pieces fit anywhere are they on their own are they a part of a different message and if we do this
one it takes an awful lot of effort an awful lot of time and awful lot of discipline and it's not going to be incredibly satisfying because many times the result is going to be something we
don't like but we're going to get multiple different objects multiple different messages and not a single
unifying message the notion that there is a single unifying message message is a postbiblical Dogma that is then
imposed upon the Bible so when people talk about looking at the picture on the box all that means is you must subordinate your interpretations to my
dogmas my traditions my ideologies and that is quite clearly putting the Dogma ahead of the data and the fit for this
video has been Dale Keon's Incredible Hulk
